run.question:
Customers reported slow checkout for the last hour. Check our Datadog APM
traces for the checkout-service and find which downstream call is slow.

report.summary: I could not identify which downstream call is slow, because no trace or latency metrics were obtainable in this run. No Datadog APM data source is available (available sources are Jaeger, Prometheus, Elasticsearch and Kubernetes; of the not_integrated list only change_history is named). Every Jaeger, Prometheus and Elasticsearch call I made failed or returned nothing usable: traces_list_services, traces_list_operations, traces_search (twice), metrics_range_query (three times), execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names and get_label_values all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, and the Elasticsearch index listing for '*' returned no indices (status no_data). Span latency, ERROR status counts and rpc_client_duration_milliseconds therefore remain unknown, not zero. The exact name 'checkout-service' never appeared; the workload present is container 'checkout' in pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n (namespace otel-demo, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout), Running and Ready with 1 restart whose last termination was exit code 255, reason 'Unknown', at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z, a timestamp shared by every otel-demo container. What I could read looked normal: all 26 otel-demo Endpoints objects have one ready address each, every flagd fault-injection flag in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config defaults to 'off', and in the newest sampled orders checkout logged 'payment went through' ~18 ms and 'email sent' ~9 ms after '[PlaceOrder]', with no error lines among the 300 lines read. Those observations neither name a slow downstream call nor clear the path customers reported; answering the question needs the trace and metric data that was unavailable.

claims.text: The checkout workload runs as container 'checkout' (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout) in pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n in namespace otel-demo; the pod is Running with all conditions True (Ready, ContainersReady), restarts=1, and its container's last termination was exitCode 255, reason 'Unknown', finishedAt 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z, with the current instance started at 2026-11-21T04:23:48Z.

A cluster-wide pod listing of 32 pods shows no pod or container named 'checkout-service': the only checkout workload is pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n with container 'checkout' in namespace otel-demo, and none of the listed pods carries an app label.

All 22 pods in namespace otel-demo show a last container termination at finishedAt 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z with exitCode 255 and reason 'Unknown' (single restart each); kube-state-metrics additionally shows exitCode 1 at 2026-11-21T04:24:17Z (restarts 2) and prometheus-readonly-proxy exitCode 1 at 2026-11-21T04:24:10Z (restarts 3). This is roughly one hour before the reported slow-checkout hour (2026-11-21T05:24:29Z–06:24:29Z).

In the newest sampled checkout log lines, the order at 06:22:03Z logged '[PlaceOrder] user_id="de2eb938-e573-11f1-812e-ae064f3c3b84" user_currency="USD"' at 2026-11-21T06:22:03.722396715Z, 'payment went through (transaction_id: 82d2cfa8-...)' at 06:22:03.740193271Z (17.8 ms later) and 'order confirmation email sent to "moore@example.com"' at 06:22:03.749619757Z (9.4 ms later); the order at 06:24:25Z shows the same pattern (about 17.8 ms then 9.1 ms). These are checkout's own log emission times, not measured downstream RPC durations.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config key demo.flagd.json defines productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad, and every one of them has defaultVariant 'off'.

In namespace otel-demo, 26 Endpoints objects each expose 1 ready address, including checkout (port 8080), cart, currency, payment, shipping, product-catalog, email, quote, recommendation and valkey-cart (6379).

The only Event inside the authorized window is a Warning FailedToCreateEndpoint on object Endpoints 'loki' at 2026-11-21T05:28:04Z with message 'Failed to create endpoint for service app-282/loki: endpoints "loki" already exists', which concerns namespace app-282/loki and not the otel-demo workloads.

Endpoint absence is not the explanation for slow checkout in the objects read now: every service in otel-demo (checkout, cart, product-catalog, currency, quote, shipping, payment, email) resolves to one ready endpoint address, so a missing backend was not observed for these dependencies at read time.

For the specific orders sampled at the end of the window, checkout's log timeline shows PlaceOrder through card charge and email completing in under about 30 ms in the 100 newest lines read, which does not show a large per-request slowdown inside checkout's own order path for those requests.

Considered and rejected as supported by the configuration read: that an enabled flagd fault-injection flag (for example paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, cartFailure, kafkaQueueProblems or imageSlowLoad) was deliberately slowing or failing a checkout dependency, because every flag in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config currently has defaultVariant 'off'. Runtime flag values pushed through flagd's API after this read are not covered.

Because checkout's own order-path log timestamps were short and error-free in the newest samples, the slowness customers reported may sit on a request path not visible in checkout's stdout (for example the frontend/frontend-proxy path or a dependency latency only visible in spans); this is unverified and could not be tested without trace or latency data.

gaps: No trace data: traces_list_services, traces_list_operations and traces_search (service 'checkout', 1h and 30m windows) all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for target m0-otel-20260909, so span-level latency per downstream call (cart, product-catalog, currency, quote/shipping, payment, email) is unknown.

No latency or error metrics: metrics_range_query (expressions over traces_span_metrics_calls_total and rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count), execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names and get_label_values all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so ERROR status counts and rpc_client_duration_milliseconds buckets are unknown, not zero.
No log-searchable store: elasticsearch_list_indices with pattern '*' returned 0 indices (status no_data), so no Elasticsearch log indices were observed in this run.
No Datadog APM data source is available in this run, so the requested Datadog APM traces for 'checkout-service' could not be queried at all.

The pod query selecting labels matching 'checkout' returned nothing (status no_data, 32 pods scanned), so pods labeled by service name could not be enumerated; only pod/container names could be matched.

The error-filtered checkout log query (filter 'error|fail|warn|timeout|deadline|unavailable|slow', 2026-11-21T05:24:29Z–06:24:29Z, limit 200) returned no matching lines (status no_data) out of 300 lines read; 194 newer lines were not shown by the earlier unfiltered read, so checkout logging no errors is unknown rather than shown.

Cause of the cluster-wide otel-demo container termination at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z (exitCode 255, reason 'Unknown', all 22 pods) is undetermined: no relevant events were returned and no kubelet or system log was available; it also predates the reported slow hour, so its relation to the slowness is unknown.
Runtime flagd state during the incident is unknown: only the ConfigMap default variants ('off') could be read; flag changes issued through the flagd API would not appear there.
Actual request latency, error rates and traffic volume for checkout and each dependency during 2026-11-21T05:24:29Z–06:24:29Z are unknown; customer-side impact was reported, not observed in this run.
Event coverage is thin: only one Event object fell inside the authorized window, so absence of rollout or failure events for otel-demo is unknown rather than disproven.
Kubernetes objects were read at approximately 2026-11-21T06:24:45Z–06:25:16Z only; their state during the incident hour cannot be reconstructed from these reads.
next_steps: Restore or re-point the Jaeger query and Prometheus scrape/proxy path for target m0-otel-20260909, then compare checkout client span durations and rpc_client_duration_milliseconds buckets per rpc_service/rpc_method for cart, product-catalog, currency, quote, shipping, payment and email over 2026-11-21T05:24Z–06:24Z against an earlier baseline window.
If Datadog is the system of record, query Datadog APM for service 'checkout-service' and break the checkout span down by downstream peer for the same hour.

Investigate why every otel-demo container terminated at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z with exit code 255 reason 'Unknown' (node/kubelet logs, container runtime logs, cluster maintenance activity) and whether collector or mesh configuration changed then.
Check flagd's runtime flag state at the incident time via feature-flag change history, since the ConfigMap defaults are all 'off' and change_history is not integrated in this run.
Once traces are available, use frontend/frontend-proxy spans to confirm whether the customer-visible slowdown originated outside checkout's own order path.

A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
